title: Mitch Evans: “I'm at a stage in my career where I'm used to winning, and I don't want that to stop.”
excerpt:
FEATURE

04 Sep 2026

6 Mins

After a decade with Jaguar, Mitch Evans is set to show up with Formula E newcomers Opel GSE next season, making it one of the biggest driver moves ahead of the GEN4 era.

During his decade in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship, Mitch Evans has been synonymous with Jaguar TCS Racing, achieving 16 victories, 38 podiums, and 10 pole positions with the British-based squad. As of the end of the 2025/26 season, the New Zealander has won the most races of any driver in the history of the all-electric championship.

The 32-year-old was also the first driver to bring home silverware for the iconic manufacturer, when he crossed the line third at the Hong Kong E-Prix in 2017. The following season, he went one step further by claiming victory in Rome, securing both his and Jaguar’s first triumph in the all-electric series.

NEWS: Opel finalises 2026/27 line-up with Mitch Evans signing

Evans has consistently delivered promising performances and has rarely been out of title contention since those early seasons. He joined Formula E at 22 years old, having just come off a GP2 series campaign in which he totalled five wins and 13 podiums - his success in the series following his championship winning GP3 season in 2012.

His arrival in the Formula E paddock would ultimately become the start of a long career, one that helped shape Evans both professionally and personally.

“I've got some more grey hair since I joined Formula E with Jaguar," he jokes. "But as a driver, as a person, we all grow older. I've been really fortunate to grow with them and the championship.

“Being in Formula E during that period has really helped me and challenged me. I look at things differently now, which obviously always comes with age. As a driver, it's really challenged me from a technical point of view, thinking outside the box, which is what Formula E is about when it comes to developing systems and software, which are areas that I never had growing up.

“Formula E is not all about going as fast as possible. There's a lot of aspects to that, it's really strengthened the way I view the championship in terms of racing and getting the most out of it. I've had some amazing memories and achievements, but some difficult periods where I've missed out on championships. I think you learn a lot about yourself in those situations, the good and bad. I'm a better driver or person than I was 10 years ago, which is the main thing, and I’m still hungry to succeed more.”

Hunger for success has always been one of Evans' greatest traits, and one that has been particularly evident in recent seasons. He has twice finished runner-up in the Drivers’ Championship, in Season 9 and Season 11, while he finished third in Season 8 and (most recently) Season 12. His latest title challenge came this year, when the New Zealander entered the London finale weekend as one of nine drivers mathematically in title contention heading into the final double-header, before the fight narrowed down to three on Sunday - Evans included.

The first half of the round saw Evans take eighth in qualifying, while his title rivals, Andretti’s Jake Dennis and Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein lined up fifth and on Pole Position, respectively. Wehrlein made the perfect start from the front of the grid, while teammate Nico Muller kept Evans behind him.

The Porsche driver capitalised on a late Full Course Yellow to take victory, adding 28 points to his tally as Dennis followed him in second. Evans, meanwhile, was left with nothing but frustration as the result left him 21 points behind in the standings.

Sunday, the final race of the GEN3 era, presented Evans with one final opportunity. Victory was the only result that would give him a realistic chance of overturning his deficit, following his costly result in the previous race.

He qualified fifth, while Wehrlein started third and Dennis could only manage 16th in his lime-green car. However, despite his best efforts, Evans was unable to produce the result he needed, finishing the race in fourth. This result left him third in the final drivers' standings with 160 points.

NEWS: Pascal Wehrlein wins his second Formula E Drivers' World Championship

But there was a silver lining, as Evans still managed to help Jaguar TCS Racing secure their second Teams’ Championship title, alongside his teammate, Antonio Felix da Costa, rounding up a total of 288 points - a final gift to the team who have played such a key role in his Formula E story.

As the championship prepares to kickstart the GEN4 era, it's most exciting era to date, Evans admits that he’s ready for a new challenge, though it means leaving a team he’s built a career and life with. “Obviously coming off the back of London, with mixed emotions. On one hand missing out on the driver's championship, and on the other hand, leaving a team that I've been with for 10 years. It was a strange feeling.

“GEN4 was a big reason why I wanted to move. I decided that I will look elsewhere, and there was some good interest from a lot of top teams. I have considered it in the past, and it's not the first time I've considered leaving Jaguar, although it's the first time I've really acted on it, I was with one team for so long, and you are always intrigued to see what other offers are out there or what other teams are up to.

“From the initial chats with Jörg (Schrott) and everyone at Opel, I felt really positive about their approach to Formula E. I visited their facilities in Satory, which really helped me, in terms of seeing their vision, seeing their resources, and seeing how seriously they're going to take the GEN4.

NEWS: Opel announces entry into Formula E from 2026/27 season

“For me it was relatively new territory for me to go down this route with another team. Opel is going to be a new team, a new brand coming to Formula E, but we have got high hopes and aspirations to hit the ground running come the season starting. I was filled with confidence, although there's an element you don't really know how it's going to go, but that comes with any decision you make.”

While the move represents a significant change for Evans, his new teammate, Theo Pourchaire is hardly an unknown quantity in motorsport. Pourchaire was crowned FIA Formula 2 champion in 2023 after finishing runner-up in the 2022 standings behind Felipe Drugovich.

“I've obviously never worked with Theo (Pourchaire) before," Evans says. "He's a few years younger than me. He's coming into Formula E at a similar age to when I did. But look, Theo's track record speaks for itself, he's had amazing success in junior formula. He was the youngest winner in F3, at 16, and he beat me by 4 days when he was in F3. I have to have a word with him about that.

“He's achieved some amazing things, and he deserves this opportunity. It's an exciting partnership because he's a rookie on paper, but he's going to come in with fresh energy, and prove himself. He's going to add a lot of value. and then obviously on my side, you've got the older guy, which is kind of weird to say, but I think he's not going to need much help in terms of getting up to speed. I'm expecting really big things from him.”

NEWS: Théo Pourchaire joins Formula E grid with Opel GSE Formula E Team

Evans had been through three generations of Formula E cars and demonstrated an ability to adapt to the championship’s constantly evolving technology. Even so, he is approaching his first season with Opel GSE with realistic expectations.

“I'm not setting any crazy targets," he says. "But we're pushing to be able to achieve podiums and ideally race wins in our first season, that'd be amazing. Do I think we can achieve it? Yes, but it's too early to say, it's a bit of a punt.

“The early signs have been really positive in terms of testing and what we're seeing amongst other teams we've been testing. We're in good shape, but there's a lot of development and a lot of things that can happen between now and the first race or throughout the season. There will be a massive development race, while we learn these cars.

“If we can keep development up, then I'm quite confident that we'll be ideally fighting at the front. I wouldn't be jumping to Opel if I didn't think that was possible. I'm at a stage in my career, where I'm used to winning, and I don't want that to stop.”

title: Lessons, podium finishes, and what comes next for Pepe Martí
excerpt:
FEATURE

03 Sep 2026

3 Mins

Pepe Martí’s debut campaign in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship established the 21-year-old CUPRA KIRO driver as 'one to watch' in the paddock!

Pepe Martí had a rookie season he could scarcely have imagined when he joined Formula E paddock at the start of the 2025/26 season. Not only did the CUPRA KIRO driver achieve two podium finishes and end the year as the highest placed rookie, but he also made history as the first Spaniard in the championship to secure a podium.

The CUPRA KIRO driver took home 66 championship points, enough to beat fellow rookie Felipe Drugovich by just one point. However, Marti narrowly missed out on a place inside the top-10, with Round 16 (the first of the London double-header finale weekend) resulting in disappointment and a point less finish. Tokyo was also a weekend of mixed emotions, with a DNF in the second race of the weekend - the day after his teammate Dan Ticktum snatched a dramatic victory from Andretti’s Jake Dennis.

“The race (Round 16 in London) ended up with a DNF, which is what you never want," said Martí. "We got quite unlucky with the Full Course Yellow. It was thrown out for about one lap so about seven cars got a really good advantage. We weren't in that group, unfortunately. We had a good pace. I was moving forward. I would have probably finished right in front of Oliver (Rowland) in P10, so we could have scraped a point, but we weren't able to. I was not happy with myself.”

“Ideally we want to finish on a good result and on the high notes as well. Most of the team is English, it's a home race for most of them. So it would’ve also been nice for them to be able to score a good result. If I'm honest today, the main limiting factor was qualifying.”

Marti responded in the following round - the final race of the 2025/26 championship campaign - taking eighth after starting from 13th on the grid (he was classified 11th in qualifying but started 13th due to a grid penalty).

Marti maintained 13th for most of the title-deciding race before completing his two ATTACK MODE activations on Lap 23 and 31. He then battled his way into the top-10 over the final four laps to take home eighth, making it a total of 128 points for CUPRA KIRO, securing the squad its most successful campaign in Formula E to date.

“I wasn’t really happy, but I guess that goes for everyone, right? Everyone apart from the winner isn't happy,” he continued. “It's not the greatest weekend of my life, but at least we got something out of it. I managed to help with people who I needed to help during the race and also finish my own race in a good position and obviously take away some points which I'm quite grateful for in this situation than I was in five races ago.

NEWS: Pepe Martí continues with CUPRA KIRO for 2026/27 season

“I have no regrets. Obviously, there are a lot of things that I would like to improve this season and I wouldn't really call it a regret. It's stuff that I want to get better at, stuff that I need to improve and obviously stuff that as a team we need to understand and move forward.”

Marti’s racecraft and determined approach to recovering from setbacks were the highlights of his debut campaign, as he managed to score nine points finishes from 17 races and proved many critics wrong. Now, however, the 21-year-old driver is ready to leave his rookie season behind and turn his attention to a new chapter for the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship - GEN4.

“We need to regroup, and come back a bit stronger next year," he asserts. “I need some time off as a whole, since 2025 even in Formula 2, I haven't had some time off and I need to sort of really, really disconnect from the motorsport world. I just want to be alone with my family, have some time off, enjoy the time with friends, the good weather, the good food, and a lot of cycling, get back in shape. In the championship, it's very hard to maintain proper shape so we can try to get better in the winter and come back stronger in December.”

Pepe Martí will continue with CUPRA KIRO for the 2025/27 Formula E season.

A further podium (a second place) followed at the 2026 Sanya E-Prix, with the additional points helping the CUPRA KIRO driver to finish the season as the highest-placed rookie in the Drivers’ Championship with 66 points.

Continuing with CUPRA KIRO, Martí will play a crucial role in the team’s next chapter as Formula E enters the GEN4 era, the most exciting chapter to date in the all-electric championship.

Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

Unleashing GEN4: A new era of high-performance, sustainable electric racing begins

3 Mins

Opel GSE has confirmed the capture of one of the most successful drivers in ABB FIA Formula E World Championship history with Mitch Evans joining the squad from the 2026/27 season.

The 32-year-old New Zealander has achieved the most victories in the racing series - 16 - and brings his experience from 10 years in the series to the new German manufacturer team.

Together with rookie Théo Pourchaire, Evans forms what Opel GSE view as a driver mix of top driver and young talent, underpinning the team's ambitions to compete at the front field from the start.

Dream team: Mitch Evans 'the preferred candidate from the beginning'

“We have secured our dream team. Mitch Evans was the preferred candidate for our Opel GSE Formula E Team from the very beginning. His commitment once again underlines the seriousness of the entire project,” said Opel Motorsport Director and Team Principal Jörg Schrott.

“We have already met Mitch on and off the racetrack. In addition to his undisputed exceptional sporting pedigree, he also fits perfectly into our team as a person. After so many years with another manufacturer, he was deliberately looking for a new challenge.

"Now the Opel family and Mitch are taking this next step together. In doing so, we are sending a clear message: We are joining the World Championship to challenge at the front.”

Evans: 'Perfect moment for a fresh challenge'

Evans himself is looking forward to the change and the cooperation with Opel. “I am proud to be an Opel works driver and to be part of this new chapter in Formula E. It’s great that we can finally make this step official,” said Evans.

“After ten years with a manufacturer, it was time for me to take on a fresh challenge. The leap to the GEN4 cars represents the perfect moment to start something new. I immediately felt how much energy and passion Opel is putting into the Formula E project.

"The team isn’t just coming into the series to compete: Opel is here to win, and that’s exactly what I aspire to.”

After a dramatic final weekend in London, Evans was narrowly denied the first Drivers' World Championship title of his career, but once again underlined his position among Formula E's best.

“The title clearly remains the big goal for me, in this respect I still have a score to settle in Formula E. That’s exactly why the move to Opel feels like the right new challenge for me.

"Starting a new Formula E generation with a new team and being successful right away is anything but a matter of course, but that’s exactly what appeals to me. I want to contribute my experience from ten years of Formula E and play a strong role in the World Championship together with Opel and Théo.”

Opel: 'Formula E the perfect stage for high-performance Mokka GSE and Corsa GSE'

Evans made his first official appearance in Opel colours this week as a surprise guest at the international media drive of the new battery-electric Opel Corsa GSE2.

This is just one example of how closely Opel is set to tie its production models with its halo motorsport project; using Formula E as a stage for its all-electric high-performance models.

After the Mokka GSE, which is already on the roads, the Corsa GSE will be launched this year and will make its trade fair debut at the Paris Motor Show in October.

The completion of the driver line-up, which includes Test and Development Driver Sophia Flörsch in addition to Evans and Pourchaire, marks Opel’s next step on the way to the World Championship.

Confirmation of its line up follows the Rüsselsheim-based manufacturer's commitment to the Opel GSE Formula E Team and the world premiere of the Opel GSE 27FE prototype at Le Castellet.

The next major milestone is coming this autumn, when Opel, together with Evans and Pourchaire, will unveil the final design of the race car for the 2026/27 season at the Paris Motor Show on 12 October 2026.

Starting 21 August, players in China will be able to take the wheel of the title-winning Porsche GEN3 99X Electric, bringing peak electric performance, high-torque acceleration, and energy recovery mechanics to Need for Speed Mobile.

Porsche GEN3 99X Electric in the Hall of Legends

Positioned in the prestigious 'Hall of Legends - Hybrid & Electric Drive' vehicle class, the Porsche GEN3 99X Electric introduces a distinct driving profile specifically calibrated to tackle the high-speed streets of Need for Speed Mobile.

Engineered to replicate the real-world dynamics of Porsche's official Formula E factory contender, the in-game machine boasts several unique handling traits:

Agile Drift Tuning: Features more agile rear-tail behavior during drifts, allowing drivers to carry higher entry speeds through tight corners and execute sharper turn-ins.

High Torque Endurance: Delivers a significantly higher base top speed, precision steering response, and automatic nitrous accumulation while cornering.

ERS Regenerative Braking System: Replicating the 99X Electric’s real-world powertrain management, the Energy Recovery System (ERS) delivers a sustained high-torque launch boost for 2.8 seconds from a standstill. During braking, handbrake turns, and inertia drifts, the system harvests kinetic energy - temporarily lowering top speed - before unleashing the stored power within 2 seconds post-drift for a massive nitrous boost

Pursuit Team Role: Drivers taking on the enforcement role will completely eliminate the helicopter cooldown timer while operating the vehicle, maintaining continuous aerial surveillance over targets.

12 years of racing and 10 different Formula E champions. Get to know them all as we prepare to enter the GEN4 era of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

Season 1 – Nelson Piquet Jr

Only one person could be crowned the inaugural champion of Formula E, and that honour went to Nelson Piquet Jr. Representing Chinese team Nextev, Piquet secured the title during the final race around London’s Battersea Park. It was a close fight between Piquet and Sebastien Buemi, with Piquet emerging on top by a single point.

During his championship-winning season, Piquet won on two occasions at Long Beach and in Moscow, in addition to podiums in Punta del Este, Buenos Aires and Monaco. He made history in becoming the very first champion in Formula E, and would continue racing with us until Season 5.

Season 2 – Sebastien Buemi

Buemi didn’t have to wait long for his turn as champion, winning the second season in truly dramatic fashion! The Swiss racer started the last race of the season in pole position, with his biggest title rival Lucas di Grassi in third. The two were tied on points, but once the lights went out Buemi and di Grassi collided.

Both cars were damaged, with the front of di Grassi’s car ruined and Buemi missing a rear wing. They both limped back to the pits, jumping into their second cars to try and snatch the fastest lap points on offer. Despite winning three races in Beijing, Punta del Este and Berlin, as well as another three podiums, it was the fastest lap in that last race that saw Buemi crowned champion in emotional scenes.

Buemi still races in Formula E, and enters Season 12 on a new multi-year contract with Envision Racing. He won last year’s Monaco E-Prix for a third time, and is tied with Jaguar TCS Racing’s Mitch Evans for the most wins in Formula E history – 14 at the time of publication.

title: Reaction from a title-deciding Formula E weekend
excerpt:
INTERVIEW

19 Aug 2026

5 Mins

The paddock reacts to a title-deciding weekend in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

Pascal Wehrlein

"Under the circumstances we had today, very special. Even though I must say the first one is always a bit more exciting. That's definitely the case, but today it was definitely a tough race. Never expected that what happened would happen, but, anyways, it is what it is. We made it.

"We set the base for today, in the last 15-16 races and we took over the lead yesterday again. The approach of the whole weekend was phenomenal, what a job we've done so far. A bit of an up-and-down season, but again, in the end, you know, when there's pressure on, when it matters, when it counts, we're pretty good.

"Obviously it was a bit unpredictable what Antonio did and how far he took it, but, you know, credits to him for what he did in this race. I think under normal circumstances during that race, we would have had a nice race, probably another podium finish, but nevertheless, I think we achieved what we had to achieve, and we did what we had to do."

Jake Dennis

"There was a clear chance. I think everything we did today, we executed perfectly. We put ourselves in a position to take the title. We were ahead at points, until we weren't. So, yeah, I think we did everything right today.

"I mean, he (Pascal) took me cleanly straight out of the race, so it's as simple as that. I think from my side, it's quite obvious. I think it's embarrassing in what we've seen today from Pascal, Porsche, to be in that position to be Pascal clearly ahead, and then he just rams me straight into the wall. It's quite surprising, but ultimately if they want to win it like that, then they can. But that's the game.

"I can leave London with my head held high. I'm happy with the way I drove, the risks I took, and yeah, I go into the off-season in a pretty good headspace. I have a lot of things personally going on in my life with my fiancée, you know, giving birth in a few weeks, so it's going to be a cool period. GEN4 is going to be exciting, and obviously I'm super busy with BMW still, so from my side an exciting few months coming up, so very much looking forward to it."

Mitch Evans

"I think ultimately we just, unfortunately, both days qualified behind the wrong car. Either a blue and white roadblock for the last two days, and they did all they could to stop me. You know, I managed to get past them in today's race, but ultimately just lost too much ground to the front guys, and yeah, it was for me a little bit extreme, but it is what it is. We did what we had to do on our side to try and give ourselves a shot, and I think we did that. But ultimately we just lost it in quali both days, but we tried and we didn't give up.

"I obviously wanted a different ending to my journey at the team, but wasn't meant to be. I don't leave with many regrets, to be fair. I knew this day was going to come at some point, especially with a lot on the line, and this team's given me so much, and I'm forever grateful for that. They've given me my first professional contract in the sport, and I owe so much to them and everyone that's been involved in the project since day one.

"I'm very proud of what we've achieved, obviously wanted more, we had one last box to check, and we unfortunately haven't done that, but a lot to be proud of. It's going to be weird waking up tomorrow not as a Jaguar driver for the first time. But I just wish them the best for the future."

Ian James (Jaguar TCS Racing)

"I'll be briefly honest, coming into this weekend, I knew how much was at stake in both championships, how much not only Mitch, but we as a team, wanted to deliver the Drivers' Championship for him and for the team as well. And there was always that risk, I suppose, that we'd let our emotions get the better of us. But all credit to the guy on my right (Evans) and to the whole team as well, because the emotions were very much kept in check.

"We approached every session with a clear and level head and executed as well as we possibly could. As Mitch said, qualifying didn't go our way, and that played a huge role then in the outcomes of both races. But at the end of the day, I'm hugely proud of both Mitch and Antonio and the whole team. It's a phenomenal way to deliver a Teams' World Championship."

Thomas Laudenbach (Porsche)

"I have to say that for us, it's great to win again the Manufacturer title. I mean, we are a car manufacturer, but we're also running a team, and but I guess it's the right time to say that this is an effort not only of our team, this is an effort of also the Andretti Formula E team, of CUPRA KIRO, and all together we scored points and secured the title. So for us, that's very important, and we're proud of that. And if you ask me how we celebrate, it's going to be a good one, I can tell you!

"This year the fight with Jaguar, I think that's what the spectators want to see, what the fans want to see. Sometimes the luck is on your side, sometimes you have bad luck. But I mean, that's sport. For today, we are, I think we can all be happy that we provided a good race today for the spectators, and extremely proud of the achievement this season."

title: Every race winner of the 2025/26 Formula E Season
excerpt:
São Paulo, Round 1

In the opening round of the 2025/26 Formula E season it was Andretti's Jake Dennis who came out on top after converting pole position into the win in the 2025 Google Cloud São Paulo E-Prix Round 1, though it was anything but a simple lights-to-flag in a hectic 30-lap race.

The Season 9 World Champion had secured Julius Baer Pole Position (following a three-place grid drop for Pascal Wehrlein) and started sharply to lead the pack away. The Brit kept in touch with the leading pack as the race lead changed hands throughout the opening stages, before making it by the Citroen of Nick Cassidy - who'd flown through the pack with a late charge - for what would be the definitive move on Lap 27.

But as the race drew to a close, there was one moment which threatened to overshadow Dennis’ charge to victory, a huge shunt for Formula E rookie Pepe Marti - who flew spectacularly over the top of Jaguar's Antonio Felix da Costa - and thankfully, ultimately, landed safely, meant a late Red Flag and a one-lap sprint to the finish. Dennis was able to hold off reigning champion Oliver Rowland and a charging Nick Cassidy to claim the first win of the season.

Mexico City, Round 2

The 2026 Hankook Mexico City E-Prix will go down in history for French manufacturing giant, Citroën, with the brand securing their first Formula E win, in only their second race in the all-electric championship - and as a nightmare for Season 2 champion, Sebastien Buemi.

REPORT: Nick Cassidy secures Citroën's first Formula E win in Mexico City

Buemi and Envision started the race from pole position, with the DS PENSKE of Taylor Barnard joining him on the front row of the grid. Barnard started well and forced Buemi into defensive manoeuvres in order to keep a hold of P1. The Swiss looked to have done just that but outbraked himself into Turn 1, eventually finding himself all the way down the order in 18th.

Instead it was Nick Cassidy, the master at picking exactly the right moment to pounce and make use of Formula E's two 50kW, all-wheel drive ATTACK MODE power boosts, who was able to take control of the race.

The New Zealander brought his Citroën home first having sliced through the pack for his fourth win in five races. Just behind him, the Mahindra of Edoardo Mortara, who had put the Kiwi under severe pressure by being one of the last drivers to activate his second ATTACK MODE.

Cassidy did hold on though for more silverware after his P3 in the Sao Paulo season-opener, with Mortara's mirrors full of reigning champion Rowland through the sweeping final turn as the top five crossed the line within a second of one-another.

Miami, Round 3

Rain came to the Sunshine State for Round 3, but it didn’t stop Mitch Evans from taking Jaguar TCS Racing’s first win of the 2025/26 season.

HIGHLIGHTS: The 2026 Miami E-Prix

The first half of the race proved to be super tricky for the pack, with polesitter Mueller leading away after a Safety Car start - though Andretti's rookie Felipe Drugovich made use of an instant all-wheel drive, 50kW ATTACK MODE activation to climb into P1 in the wet early on.

Mueller found himself back out front after the first round of ATTACK MODE and was able to take advantage of a mishap - as the rain fell harder - between Drugovich and Jaguar TCS Racing's Antonio Felix da Costa behind that took the pair out of race-winning contention.

Amid all that, Evans spied his chance to make progress - clambering through from the back end of the top 10 to the podium positions before a perfect switchback move on Lap 27 saw him by Mueller - the German falling for the dummy move.

From there, the Kiwi was able to manage the lead through the second round of ATTACK MODE activations to a commanding 3.1-second lead come the chequered flag for a record 15th Formula E race win.

Jeddah, Round 4

Formula E returned to Jeddah for Round 4 of the championship and the first double-header of the season. In his 100th E-Prix, Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein sealed a perfectly-executed victory, timing his PIT BOOST and ATTACK MODE just right to head home Mahindra Racing's Edoardo Mortara and Jaguar Racing driver Mitch Evans.

READ: Everything you need to know about PIT BOOST in Formula E

Wehrlein had started the race third and went later than those around him with his 50kW, all-wheel drive ATTACK MODE boost coming after his PIT BOOST stop.The overlap allowed the Season 10 World Champion to pull some eight seconds on those behind heading into the closing stages of the race.

Those who activated ATTACK MODE late seemed the best placed as the race reached its climax. Evans was next to prove as much as he sliced his way through the top 10 to an eventual third at the chequered flag and back-to-back podiums.

Jeddah, Round 5

Antonio Felix da Costa and Jaguar TCS Racing nailed their race strategy to stride to the race win in the 2026 Jeddah E-Prix Round 5, with the Portuguese leading Sebastien Buemi home and reigning champion Oliver Rowland rounding out the podium.

Da Costa was the first of the lead group to leap for both of his mandatory 50kW, all-wheel drive ATTACK MODE boosts and managed to pull a gap on those behind through the second round of activations - enough to hold fast for the win with 2.5 seconds to spare at the chequered flag. Six races in nine for Jaguar and da Costa's first for the team as well as his first since Portland, 2024.

Several drivers cycled the race lead in an energy-critical race, with Buemi one of those - the Swiss eventually winding up second, using an ATTACK MODE overlap to best Rowland who had also led early on.

Madrid, Round 6

Antonio Felix da Costa (Jaguar TCS Racing) became the first and only driver to take more than one victory this season when he stormed to his 14th career win around the Circuito del Jarama.

READ: DAC-TO-DAC: Jaguar's Da Costa debriefs epic Madrid win

Having started third, the 2019/20 Formula E Champion perfectly timed his PIT BOOST and ATTACK MODE activation to rise to the top of the pack. He was on the defensive across the final laps with challenges for the win from his teammate Mitch Evans, CUPRA KIRO’s Dan Ticktum, Porsche’s Pascal Wehrlein and Mahindra Racing’s Edoardo Mortara.

It made for blockbuster viewing, with the grandstands and grassy banks around the circuit packed to the brim with passionate Spanish fans. With Da Costa being Portuguese, and Lisbon a six hour drive from the capital city, he was surrounded by family and friends across the weekend.

Wehrlein leads the Drivers' Championship on 83 points - 11 points clear of Mahindra Racing's Edoardo Mortara. In the Teams' Championship it's tight, with Porsche only 4 points ahead of Jaguar TCS Racing.

Berlin, Round 7

Nico Müller secured a historic maiden victory during the first race of the Berlin E-Prix double-header. On his 69th start in Formula E, the Swiss driver delivered a strategic masterclass to win Porsche's home race in dominant fashion.

Starting from 6th on the grid, Müller focused on energy management during a chaotic opening half, but after his PIT BOOST he made the most of his energy advantage to slice through the grid and build an impressive lead with help from his ATTACK MODE. He finished 4.7 seconds clear of the field to seal a home victory for Porsche and his very first in Formula E, a special moment he shared with his family.

The win was particularly symbolic as Porsche was celebrating the 75th anniversary of Porsche Motorsport. To mark the occasion, Müller’s car ran a special "Pink Pig" livery, a tribute to the legendary Porsche 917/20 from the 1971 24 Hours of Le Mans!

Berlin, Round 8

Jaguar TCS Racing's Mitch Evans timed his push to perfection to take victory at Tempelhof ahead of reigning champion Oliver Rowland and Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein.

The New Zealander started 17th and clambered to the top six by the end of the first round of ATTACK MODE activations with energy in-hand on those around him.

RACE HIGHLIGHTS: 2026 Hankook Berlin E-Prix, Round 8

His initial six-minute 50kW, all-wheel drive ATTACK saw him hit the front on Lap 27 and take control from there, building a gap of two seconds to those behind. He swatted the advances of two World Champions in Rowland and Wehrlein away through the second round of ATTACK MODE as the race reached its climax to seal the deal and his 16th race win in Formula E - more than any other driver in the series' history.

Monaco, Round 9

Mahindra Racing's Nyck de Vries kept his cool around the tight and twisty streets of Monaco to claim his fifth ABB Formula E World Championship race victory, ahead of Jaguar Racing's Mitch Evans and CUPRA KIRO's Pepe Marti.

The Dutch driver started on the front row of the grid, eventually taking the lead of the race with a perfectly executed PIT BOOST strategy, which saw him finish the E-Prix with a comfortable gap to the chasing pack.

De Vries was one of the first drivers to take his PIT BOOST stop, diving into the pits on Lap 16. From there, he smartly timed his ATTACK MODE activation, overtaking then-race leader Antonio Felix da Costa on Lap 20 and remaining unfazed by the fraught battles happening in and around him. From there, he was unchallenged, reaching the chequered flag with a three second gap to the cars behind.

RESULTS: The 2026 Monaco E-Prix Round 9

The victory marks a fifth career win for de Vries, and his first since Berlin 2022 as well as a maiden win with Mahindra - a first for the Indian team in the GEN3 era.

Monaco, Round 10

Nissan's Oliver Rowland assembled the perfect E-Prix to seal victory in Round 10 of the 2025/26 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship in Monaco - navigating the drama to lead home Felipe Drugovich (Andretti) and Antonio Felix da Costa (Jaguar TCS Racing).

Rowland started eighth and came to the fore late on as the ATTACK MODE activations shook out - with the top 10 shuffling and squabbling relentlessly for position throughout the opening half of the race.

The Nissan driver had been strong managing his energy, navigated the pack and picked his way through to the lead down at the Nouvelle Chicane on Lap 23 of 28 - classic Rowland and a second win in two years in Monte Carlo for the Brit.

RESULTS: The 2026 Monaco E-Prix Round 10

A couple of Full Course Yellows were thrown into the mix for Rowland to deal with after some overexhuberant overtaking manoeuvres down the field but the Nissan driver kept cool to cross the line first.

Sanya, Round 11

Jake Dennis and Felipe Drugovich finished as they'd started - with plenty of drama in-between - in the Lianxin Sanya E-Prix Round 11, sealing American team Andretti's first 1-2 in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

The pair steered through a Red Flag and two Full Course Yellows having led away from the front row of the grid to work together and dictate early on. Going later in ATTACK proved to be the way to go as they stamped their authority on the race through the first third and then, most importantly, in the lead up to the chequered flag - having dropped into the pack midway through the encounter.

That was a second win of the season for the Season 9 World Champion, and the second from Julius Baer Pole Position, too. The team followed up a first front-row lockout with that maiden 1-2. CUPRA KIRO's Pepe Marti produced a wonder-drive from all but last at the Red Flag restart to third in effectively just 17 racing laps - the Spaniard also following up maiden silverware in Monte Carlo with another trophy here.

UPDATE: Drugovich hit with five-second time penalty, loses podium finish

However, there was more drama to come after the flag. Drugovich was hit with a five-second time penalty for contact with Wehrlein that was judged to have been avoidable by race stewards. This meant that Marti was promoted to a career-best second place, while Nyck de Vries inherited third position.

Shanghai, Round 12

Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein strode to victory in the Shanghai E-Prix Round 12, timing PIT BOOST to perfection, just before the weather closed in - ending the German's three-race pointless streak.

The polesitter won the battle for track position, as drivers and engineers pushed for the front with rain on the horizon. Heading through the PIT BOOST window, he emerged out front before a Safety Car was required as the rain fell hard on Lap 19.

The Season 10 World Champion was able to stride clear of the pack from there to the chequered flag with Antonio Felix da Costa (Jaguar TCS Racing) and Jake Dennis (Andretti) unable to prevent Wehrlein sealing a 10th career victory.

RESULTS: The 2026 Shanghai E-Prix Round 12

Felipe Drugovich followed Dennis home as the Andrettis played the team game to secure P3 and P4 through the final few laps. Nyck de Vries followed for Mahindra, climbing all the way from P16 to fifth at the flag. Jean-Eric Vergne came sixth after a tidy E-Prix for Citroen Racing.

Shanghai, Round 13

Drying conditions favoured the brave as those that gambled with the setup on their cars were able to slice through the field to the podium, and none profited more than ultra-experienced Brazilian Lucas di Grassi who had started the race in 18th position.

Joel Eriksson (Envision Racing) had led the pack away from a late caution with Jean-Eric Vergne (Citroen Racing) and di Grassi in close company - the trio all up 16 spots from the start at this stage. Crucially, that Full Course Yellow had neutralised Eriksson and Vergne's ATTACK MODE activations, with di Grassi's still in-hand.

RESULTS: The 2026 Shanghai E-Prix Round 13

The 2016/17 champion duly used his remaining 50kW, all-wheel drive boost once the FCY ended to make up ground on the pair ahead, passing Eriksson at the hairpin on the penultimate lap as Vergne fought through to the lead - before dispatching the Citroen driver half a lap later at Turn 1, on the final lap, for the win.

That was a first trip to the top step of the podium since 2022 for di Grassi, who also won the very first Formula E race, also here in China back in 2014. He remains Formula E's oldest race winner at now 41 years 328 days old and he sets a new record as the series' oldest podium finisher. Vergne came home second in the end with Eriksson following for his best finish yet, and a maiden podium.

Tokyo, Round 14

CUPRA KIRO's Dan Ticktum pounced through the penultimate corner to steal victory from Jake Dennis in the first Tokyo night race; with the pair heading home Nick Cassidy who sealed an emotional podium for Citroen Racing in the 2026 TDK Tokyo E-Prix Round 14.

Ticktum started sixth and went early with both PIT BOOST and ATTACK MODE to emerge from the stops as the net leader. Dennis, though, had the overlap on the rest with his 50kW, all-wheel drive boost and by the end of Lap 29, he made it by Cassidy then Ticktum to hit the front. From there, it looked to be comfortable, with Ticktum also seeming to settle for a strong second with a message over Team Radio.

RESULTS: The 2026 TDK Tokyo E-Prix Round 14

However, right at the last - through the penultimate turn, ahead of the final chicane, Ticktum spied his chance to jump Dennis as the Andretti driver lifted early with energy critical. He made the move stick and led his compatriot home to make it nine different winners in the last nine rounds, with the closest winning margin of the season - his second in Formula E.

Tokyo, Round 15

Mahindra Racing's Nyck de Vries got his setup just right to fire from fifth to victory in the 2026 TDK Tokyo E-Prix Round 15 in mixed conditions, heading home Citroen Racing's Nick Cassidy and Andretti's Jake Dennis, with title contenders Pascal Wehrlein and Mitch Evans failing to score.

De Vries made a timely jump for ATTACK on Lap 28 and picked off those ahead to reach reigning champion Oliver Rowland in P1; the Nissan driver himself on a late charge. The Brit elected not to match de Vries up with his own final of two mandatory 50kW all-wheel drive ATTACK MODE activations, and that proved costly as de Vries made it by Rowland through the middle sector of that same tour.

RESULTS: The 2026 TDK Tokyo E-Prix Round 15

Mahindra had opted to set the car up for a drying surface, gambling on further rain holding off after a deluge earlier in the afternoon. De Vries navigated a late Red Flag for a second win of 2025/26 and Mahindra's second of the season; a feat the team hadn't achieved since 2017/18.

Dennis, staggeringly, clambered from 17th to the final spot on the podium thanks to a late ATTACK MODE charge. That sees him top of the Drivers' World Championship heading to the site of his first title victory in London and the finale weekend.

The Season 9 champion was able to take advantage of Pascal Werhlein's misery, with a second non-score for the Porsche driver in as many rounds in Tokyo leaving him third in the running. Mitch Evans (Jaguar TCS Racing) failed to finish today, too, and having provisionally led the running earlier in the race, he leaves Tokyo two points behind Dennis in second.

London, Round 16

Polesitter Wehrlein's ultimately dominant third win of the season was sealed during the PIT BOOST window. Werhlein was able to make use of a timely Full Course Yellow (FCY) - thrown for the recovery of Lucas di Grassi's Lola Yamaha ABT - to make what effectively became a free pit stop with the pack neutralised by the caution.

RESULTS: The 2026 Hankook London E-Prix Round 16

Mitch Evans had been looking to mount a challenge from third despite the Porsches of Wehrlein and Mueller working together, against him, early on. Jaguar TCS Racing switched up his strategy to clear Mueller with an early ATTACK MODE deployment and PIT BOOST stop - forcing leader Werhlein to counter. The FCY put paid to Evans' charge, though, and left the Kiwi marooned 21 points back in the standings in third spot.

Dennis was another of several drivers that pitted during FCY and elected to take his ATTACK late to clamber from the cusp of the top six to second at the flag with moves by da Costa and Ticktum key in limiting Wehrlein's new gap at the top of the Drivers' standings to five points.

London, Round 17

The destination of the crown changed hands three times in as many corners, as Andretti's Jake Dennis made a late charge from the back of the pack with Wehrlein coming under severe pressure from Antonio Felix da Costa (Jaguar TCS Racing), who did his bit in his teammate's fight for the title, and in Jaguar's battle for Teams' honours.

At the end of Lap 27, Wehrlein was told by his race engineer to let a charging Sebastien Buemi (Envision Racing) past but that, and a squeeze from da Costa, left the pre-race standings leader shuffled all the way to 12th and outside the points with Dennis able to make it by for eighth, enough to the top of the points table, through his first ATTACK MODE while Evans sat fourth.

Ultimately, Evans could climb no higher, having bided his time to take ATTACK MODE; the Mahindras and Barnard had gapped the Jaguar driver and the rest out-front. A win was the only outcome that would have seen the Kiwi take the crown, even with Wehrlein being once again shuffled down the order and out of the points-paying positions by his own contact with Envision Racing's Joel Eriksson at Turn 16 on Lap 31.

The ensuing chaos handed caught out Dennis too, and the Brit was eliminated from the race and title contention with damage to his car caused in the melee.

Barnard's late ATTACK MODE activation saw him able to muscle by Mortara for P2, then polesitter de Vries for the win with a sneaky dive up the inside of the Season 8 champion into the final turn with just two laps left to run. The Brit was able to convert to become the youngest Formula E race winner at 22 years and 76 days old, superseding Maximilian Guenther, on DS Automobiles final Formula E outing.

title: History in the making: Taylor Barnard becomes Formula E’s youngest winner
excerpt:
FEATURE

18 Aug 2026

2 Mins

On the day that Formula E crowned a new champion, DS PENSKE's Taylor Barnard made some history of his own.

Youngest driver to start a Formula E race, youngest pole sitter and youngest driver to claim a podium. Heading into the final race weekend of the 2025/26 season, DS PENSKE's Taylor Barnard was missing just one record (and arguably the most important one) - to be named Formula E's youngest race winner.

REPORT: Wehrlein navigates dramatic finale to seal Drivers' title as Barnard wins in London

Barnard joined the French squad at the start of the season, following NEOM McLaren's exit from the championship, and despite showing moments of promise and raw pace over the course of the 2025/26 campaign, he has struggled to replicate the impressive points scoring haul of his rookie year.

But heading into the final day of the season, with most eyes on the fight at the head of the championship, British-born Barnard quietly put together a confident and assured performance in qualifying, placing him 6th on the grid for the E-Prix. In the race, Barnard remained in contention throughout, closely following the Mahindra Racing duo of Nyck de Vries and Edoardo Mortara.

The winning moment came in the closing stages of the race, when Barnard's late ATTACK MODE activation saw him able to muscle by Mortara for P2, then polesitter de Vries for the win with a sneaky dive up the inside of the Season 8 champion into the final turn with just two laps left to run.

"I think playing around the championship games was obviously important," said Formula E's newest race winner. "As soon as I got to P3 and I had Antonio behind me, I knew there was going to be some games going on, so it almost felt like a podium secured at that point. And then I was just trying to do everything I can to get as much advantage on the Mahindras as possible.

I didn't think it was going to be possible, they both had two minutes more energy. So, yeah, to be able to get both of them, honestly, is unreal."

At 22 years and 76 days old, Barnard becomes the youngest race winner in Formula E history, taking the record from his DS PENSKE teammate Maximilian Gunther, who won the 2020 Santiago E-Prix at 22 years and 200 days old. And after a long season of highs and lows, surely the result gives the young Brit a big dose of confidence heading into the off season.

"I've now got two complete seasons in Formula E under my belt," he says. "And it's been a long learning process, but obviously the longer I'm going, the more experience I'm getting and the better I'm getting generally at the races, so it's going to keep going. But obviously, it's a massive confidence boost for the team as well. It's been such a tough season, so everybody deserves it."

Taylor Barnard finishes the 2025/26 season 11th in the Drivers' Championship on 68 points.

title: HANKOOK DEBRIEF: Five things we learned in London
excerpt:
FEATURE

17 Aug 2026

5 Mins

Championship Journalist Katy Fairman picks her five top talking points from a busy season finale in London.

Feature by Katy Fairman

The 2026 Hankook London E-Prix double-header at the London Excel marked the end of several eras across the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship – from racing retirements, first-time winners, and the last running of the GEN3 era, here are five storylines defined the weekend.

Tense and tight championship battle

The 2025/26 Drivers’ and Teams’ World Championship title race came down to the absolute wire, with both accolades being decided in the final laps of the final race.

Heading into the season finale weekend, the top three contenders of Jake Dennis (Andretti), Mitch Evans (Jaguar TCS Racing), and Pascal Wehrlein (Porsche) were separated by just five points. Wehrlein took the advantage in Saturday’s Round 16 by securing the Julius Baer Pole Position and victory, as Dennis finished second and Evans found himself the victim of an unfortunately timed Full Course Yellow.

However, come Sunday, Wehrlein couldn’t manage back-to-back poles and instead started behind a first-ever Mahindra front-row lockout. Despite starting fourth and having teammate Nico Müller behind, Wehrlein eventually fell back in the pack until he found himself alongside his championship rival Jake Dennis. The two made contact, with Dennis going into the wall and out of the points which handed advantage to Wehrlein – meanwhile Evans tried to fight his way to the front as the only way to win his first drivers’ crown was to finish in first place and both Wehrlein and Dennis to be out of the points.

Evans could only manage fourth at the flag, and with Wehrlein and Dennis out of the points after their coming together, it meant it was the Porsche of Wehrlein who became only the second driver in Formula E’s 12 year history to become a double champion.

In the Teams’ title, it was Jaguar TCS Racing who took the honours thanks to a brilliant effort all season by Evans and his teammate Antonio Felix da Costa. It was a particularly emotional effort from the Jaguar team, as they bid farewell to Mitch Evans who has been racing for the team since he entered the all-electric championship a decade – and 143 race starts – ago.

Barnard breaks more records

Following his debut win in London, DS PENSKE’s Taylor Barnard became the youngest driver to win a Formula E race at 22 years and 76 days old. It’s a record he could only have secured at that race in London, as by the time we get back racing in GEN4 the record couldn’t have been broken, and the Brit delivered.

That’s now another statistic for Barnard, after being the youngest driver to start a race, youngest points scorer, youngest podium finisher and youngest pole sitter – all in Formula E.

The win comes after a challenging season for the DS PENSKE squad, and in the final race where DS will be participating after they announced their departure earlier this year. It also means that every single Formula E team recorded at least one podium this season, and all but one team – Envision – managed a victory.

One more time

It was the final race weekend for former Formula E driver Lucas di Grassi, who announced his retirement from racing earlier this season with Lola Yamaha ABT. The Brazilian was one of the first drivers to confirm his participation in the series, and has started 165 E-Prix during those 12 seasons. ABT are also ending their time in the championship, after several successful seasons in Formula E over the years.

As well as his departure, it was also the final race for 2015/16 champion Sebastien Buemi who announced ahead of the weekend that he’ll be stepping down from a full-time race seat by continuing with the team in an advisor and development role in GEN4. His Envision teammate Joel Eriksson was also confirmed to not be resuming his racing driver role at the team from next season.

Norman Nato shared that his last race in Formula E with Nissan was in London, with Maximilian Guenther also confirming the news that he was leaving DS PENSKE ahead of the next generation of Formula E. There are also question marks over Dan Ticktum, who – after winning in Tokyo last month – reminded people he was a ‘free agent’ with no seat promised for next season.

It was also the last event for Hankook – also the title sponsor of the event – who have been providing the championship with tyres for the entire GEN3 era.

Last dance at the London Excel

This past weekend marked Formula E’s final appearance at the popular Excel Docklands venue, which has hosted the event on its unique indoor-outdoor track since the 2020/2021 season. It’s been a venue that has seen championships crowned, plenty of home heroes achieving wins, podiums and pole positions, as well as smashing a Guinness World Record for setting the world record for the fastest speed achieved by a vehicle indoors.

Formula E car hits 218km/h indoors to smash Guinness World Record

Starting from next year, the London E-Prix will find a new home at Brands Hatch with the legendary circuit, situated in Kent – 30 minutes outside London – welcomes Formula E for the first time.

A new way to watch for GEN4

Off the track, Formula E announced a major global streaming partnership with Disney+ and ESPN+ from next season.The landmark multi-year agreement brings every Formula E race live across 144 territories, including the US, The agreement marks one of the most significant milestones in Formula E’s history, bringing together Disney’s unrivalled global entertainment platforms with the world’s leading all-electric motorsport championship.

Majority-owned by Liberty Global, Formula E will leverage Disney’s global streaming ecosystem to reach millions of new households while complementing its established portfolio of free-to-air and linear broadcast partners around the world, ensuring fans continue to enjoy broad access across key markets.

Launching alongside the revolutionary GEN4 era, the collaboration will introduce Formula E to millions of new fans through Disney+ while preserving the broad accessibility that has underpinned the series' success to date.

Saudi Arabia has been named the first-ever recipient of Formula E's brand-new "Best Host Country" award, recognizing the Kingdom's outstanding contribution to delivering one of the world's leading electric motorsport championships.

Presented for the first time in the all-electric championship’s history during the 2025/26 Season Formula E End of Season Awards in London last night, the accolade recognizes the destination that sets the global benchmark for event delivery, infrastructure and partnership.

The Kingdom’s recognition with this prestigious award stands as a testament to its excellence in hosting the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship and to the advanced standards it has established since first hosting the Championship in 2018.

This achievement also reflects the unwavering support extended to the sports sector by the Kingdom’s leadership, under the guidance of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz, Crown Prince and Prime Minister, may Allah protect them. It further reflects the support of His Royal Highness Prince Abdulaziz bin Turki Al Faisal, Minister of Sport; the continued efforts of the Ministry of Sport; and the operational excellence delivered by the Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation, Saudi Motorsport Company, and Sela.

Eng. Mansour Almokbel, Acting CEO of the Saudi Automobile & Motorcycle Federation (SAMF) and CEO of the Saudi Motorsport Company (SMC), said: "We sincerely thank Formula E for this recognition.

"Receiving the Formula E ‘Best Host Country’ award is the result of the collective efforts of everyone who has contributed to hosting and delivering the championship’s races in the Kingdom, from its beginnings in Diriyah through to Jeddah.

"It is a testament to Saudi Arabia’s commitment to staging world-class motorsport events and reflects the strength of our partnerships, expertise and dedication, which continue to elevate the Kingdom’s position on the global motorsport stage.

"Our vision extends far beyond hosting international championships. We are building a sustainable motorsport ecosystem that will inspire future generations, develop Saudi talent and create lasting opportunities across the industry.

"Every event we host is another step towards strengthening Saudi Arabia's position as a global hub for motorsport, and awards such as this reinforce our commitment to continually raising the benchmark for excellence."

Alberto Longo, Co-Founder & Chief Championship Officer of Formula E, said: "The unwavering support and long-term partnership of the Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation, the Saudi Motorsport Company and Ministry of Sport have been instrumental to our journey since 2018.

"Their vital role has helped establish Formula E as a global leader in both motorsport and international events across the Kingdom. Formula E remains deeply aligned to the goals of Vision 2030 and shared vision for a sustainable future.

"We are deeply grateful for their continued commitment, and it is a well-deserved honour to see them recognised with Formula E's inaugural ‘Best Host Country’ award. We look forward to many more years of innovation together."

Saudi Arabia's partnership with Formula E has continued to go from strength to strength since 2018. Following the race’s move from Diriyah to Jeddah in 2025, the inaugural Jeddah E-Prix became the most-watched Formula E race weekend in history, attracting a record 65 million cumulative global viewers.

Jeddah also played a pioneering role in the Championship's continued evolution when it became the first venue to introduce Formula E's innovative PIT BOOST feature in Season 11, with mandatory mid-race pit stops debuting during the Kingdom's double-header before being rolled out across all subsequent double-header events during the season.

Building on a legacy of firsts that has come to define the Kingdom's place in global motorsport, Saudi Arabia will host the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship’s 2026/27 Season opening double-header weekend on December 18–19, 2026 and continue its tradition of delivering landmark moments for Formula E. The event will mark the competitive debut of Formula E's revolutionary GEN4 race car, ushering in a new era for the all-electric championship with faster performance, greater efficiency and enhanced racing.

As Saudi Arabia celebrates this achievement, the Kingdom looks ahead to many more years of partnership with Formula E, delivering world-class racing, pioneering innovation, and unforgettable experiences that continue to elevate the championship on the global stage.

The German has announced he'll move on, as DS Automobiles' longstanding spell as a brand in Formula E - most recently alongside the PENSKE operation - drew to a close at the conclusion of the London finale.

Maximilian Günther has announced that he'll be leaving DS PENSKE following the conclusion of the 2025/26 campaign in London this past weekend.

DS Automobiles is one of the most decorated manufacturers in Formula E history, famously becoming the first brand to secure back-to-back double titles.

Joining the series in Season 2, the marque secured four titles, 19 victories, and 55 podiums across 151 races.

Taylor Barnard ensured the team signed off in style with a finale victory in London.

The Brit became the youngest-ever race winner in Formula E history at 22 years and 76 days with his penultimate lap move on Nyck de Vries (Mahindra) for the win in Round 17.
